cells.tense: You are holding what was handed to you and letting it shift with the people across from you right now.
cells.act: add a little or take a little away, and sense the difference
cells.ask: In what you pass on, change the wording or the order. Sit with whether it landed, then stop. No week to keep, no tally.
cells.core:
You hold something that came from somewhere and you carry it forward, and none of it is stiff. You can read what the person sitting with you needs and you give them that, not the whole archive. Nothing splits you off from what you hold. That is why it keeps moving instead of wearing thin. The words shift, the core stays, and people take what is theirs without pretending to be the same as anybody else.

When the line you're passing on doesn't suit the person beside you, adjust it — the wording, the order, what you leave out — then stop fussing. One small turn of the dial, then let it run. What you're holding is stronger when it moves a little with the moment. Nothing here needs adding or subtracting wholesale; it needs the small correction that keeps it alive.
cells.sheetLine: What you hold stays alive because you let it shift.
cells.place: a place where things are calibrated as they move

cells.tense: You are bracing against a moment that hasn't come, holding the shape of the thing like it will break if anyone breathes on it.
cells.act: stop holding up the false thing and watch it come down
cells.ask: Pick the rule you're propping up by hand, then take your hand away. Let it lean where it leans and don't rebuild. Then leave it.
cells.core:
What you're carrying has become a rule. The core is right — the thing did hold once, and it matters — but the way you hold it now demands that people stand the same way, and they can feel the pressure coming off it. The windows have been sealed to keep the air even. That isn't the thing itself; it's the scaffolding you've built around it, and the scaffolding is heavy enough to be felt by whoever walks past.

Find the piece you're holding up that wouldn't stand without your hand under it. Take your hand away. Let it lean or fall, and don't catch it. What comes down comes down, and what stays was the thing itself. You'll be able to tell the difference once your arms are free of the weight.
cells.sheetLine: You are holding a shape up that only stands because you hold it.

cells.tense: You've been alone in this a long while, building every piece yourself because none of it was handed to you.
cells.act: step back far enough to see the whole arrangement
cells.ask: Choose a stretch of your own working-out and step back. See the parts and how they bear on each other. No notes, no verdict on it.
cells.core:
You've been putting the pieces together from scratch — every frame, every use — because nobody handed anything over when it was needed. The work you've done inside that is real; the price is that it's yours alone, and there's nowhere to set it down. Standing on your own ground has meant standing on no ground. There's no history behind the way you know things, so it's hard to say whether any of it counts as anything but yours.

Take some working-out of your own. Not the biggest thing. Step back and look at how it runs underneath — no detail, just the arrangement. What are the parts, and how do they bear on each other? Once you can see the shape, it stops being only yours. It can be handed on, and it can hold you.

cells.tense: You are already moving the thing forward, and your phrase for it is that you're just getting along.
cells.act: find the centre and hold it while things move
cells.ask: When something needs a small correction with someone and you make it, pause one breath first and let your own hand in it register. Then carry on.
cells.core:
There's something being carried forward through you. You adjust when it needs adjusting — a word changed here, a weight taken off one side and put on the other — and it works, which is why nobody, including you, has looked at it. Your phrase for it is that you're easy to be around. The balancing has your handwriting on it. You'd say the group just gets on well, and what's actually happening is that the small corrections come off your hand minute to minute without ever being marked.

Next time you sense the shift and make it, pause for one breath first and let yourself register that the hand doing it is yours. Then do it, or leave it. Either is fine. That pause is the only distance between being carried along by the thing and holding its centre while it moves.
cells.sheetLine: You are keeping it steady, and your phrase for it is getting along.
